news.Title: Can Semtech's 1.6T Ramp Accelerate its Data Center Growth?
news.Content:
Semtech Corporation SMTC is seeing strong demand for its data center products as hyperscalers increase spending on AI infrastructure. The company's data center revenues reached a record $100 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 39% sequentially and 91% year over year. Growth was driven by continued strength in 800G products, along with the ramp of 1.6T CopperEdge and FiberEdge solutions. Management expects this momentum to continue, with data center revenues projected to increase 45% sequentially and 160% year over year in the third quarter of fiscal 2027.

The 1.6T transition could become an important growth driver for Semtech. Management expects 1.6T FiberEdge and CopperEdge products to account for more than 50% of total data center revenues in the third quarter of fiscal 2027. Semtech is also gaining market share in optical connectivity, where its FiberEdge business has grown from about 18% market share in 800G two years ago to more than 50%. Further, the company expects its 1.6T FiberEdge market share to exceed 50% by the end of fiscal 2027.

The company is also preparing for the next stage of data center growth. Semtech is expanding its photonics portfolio through gain chips, high-power CW lasers, semiconductor optical amplifiers and photodiodes. These products are aimed at higher-speed applications, including 3.2T transceivers and co-packaged optics. Management expects its content per transceiver to increase from high single-digit dollars to high double-digit dollars as data center speeds move from 800G to 3.2T.

Strong customer demand supports SMTC's prospects as well, with the company reporting that its backlog for the remainder of fiscal 2027 was fully booked and more than 70% of its target for fiscal 2028 was already covered. Management is also working with manufacturing partners to secure additional capacity for fiscal 2028 and beyond. If it can meet customer requirements and maintain its product momentum, the 1.6T ramp could remain an important driver of Semtech's data center growth over the next several quarters.

How Competitors Fare Against SMTC

Semtech faces stiff competition from Marvell Technology MRVL and MACOM Technology Solutions MTSI in high-speed data center connectivity.

MRVL offers optical digital signal processors, switching products, transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs) and drivers for high-speed optical connectivity. Its data center revenues reached a record $2.17 billion in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 46% year over year. Demand for its 800G products remains strong, while its 1.6T business is ramping rapidly. The company now expects fiscal 2027 revenues to grow about 45% year over year to roughly $12 billion, with data center revenues up about 60%.

Story Continues

MTSI is also expanding its presence in high-speed data center connectivity. Its portfolio includes 800G and 1.6T products, linear equalizers for copper interconnects, high-speed TIAs and drivers, and photodetectors. Data center remained MTSI's fastest-growing business in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, with revenues of $137.6 million, up about 40% sequentially and 81.5% year over year. The company reported a record book-to-bill ratio of 1.6 in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 and expects fiscal 2026 data center growth of about 74%.

news.Title: Micron's HBM4 Ramp-Up: Can Higher Pricing Lift Margins Further?
news.Content:
Micron Technology, Inc. MU is positioned to benefit from the rising demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) as AI companies build more powerful data centers. Its HBM4 ramp-up could support further margin growth if strong demand, higher prices and efficient production continue.

Micron's fourth-quarter 2026 revenues jumped 379.3% year over year to $54.23 billion, while the full fiscal 2026 top line surged 256.3% to $133.19 billion. The fourth-quarter non-GAAP gross margin reached 87%, up from 45.7% in the year-ago quarter. The company's full fiscal 2026 gross margin reached 81.1% from 41.1% in fiscal 2025, highlighting the benefits of favorable memory pricing and strong demand.

HBM is an important part of this opportunity. Micron reported that HBM revenues grew faster than total company revenues in the fourth quarter. It has also completed agreements covering most of its HBM bit supply for calendar year 2027, with significantly higher prices than the previous year. These agreements offer better revenue visibility and could help support profitability as shipments increase.

Micron's HBM4 progress adds another growth opportunity. The company said its 12-high HBM4 production ramp-up is advancing twice as fast as the comparable HBM3E generation, and it has already shipped more than $1 billion in HBM4 revenues. Faster production growth and better manufacturing yields could help reduce costs and improve returns as volumes rise.

Pricing is another potential margin driver. Micron has secured most of its 2027 HBM supply agreements at significantly higher year-over-year prices. Management expects these prices to narrow the gross-margin gap between HBM and conventional DRAM. However, the actual benefit will depend on production costs, product yields and how quickly shipments increase.

Micron's HBM4 ramp-up and higher contract prices provide a strong foundation for further margin improvement. Its 87% fourth-quarter gross margin already reflects favorable market conditions, but sustaining such high levels will depend on execution and continued AI spending. For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Micron expects non-GAAP gross margin of approximately 86.25%.

How Do Rivals Fare Against Micron in AI Memory Space?

Micron's major competitors, SK hynix SKHY and Sandisk Corporation SNDK, are also benefiting from AI-led demand for memory and storage solutions.

SK hynix is one of Micron's closest DRAM rivals and has a strong position in HBM, which is critical for AI accelerators. In the second quarter of 2026, SK hynix generated 79.3 trillion Korean won in revenues, up 257% year over year, while operating profit surged 557% to 60.5 trillion won. HBM, AI-server DRAM and enterprise SSDs drove the strong results.

Story Continues

Sandisk is more focused on NAND and storage than DRAM, but it is another stock that stands to benefit from AI infrastructure spending. Its fiscal 2026 revenues jumped 175% to $20.25 billion, while data-center revenues soared 437% to $5.15 billion. Sandisk's fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 revenues also surged 372% sequentially to $8.97 billion, showing strong demand for storage products used in data centers.

Both companies highlight the broadening AI-driven demand for memory and storage, although Micron remains particularly well-positioned in DRAM and HBM.

news.Title: Why It’s Time to Load Up on Marvell Stock
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (MRVL) shares have had an outstanding run, gaining around 224% year-to-date. While the rally has made the stock more expensive, its strong growth outlook suggests room for further gains.

The core thesis for buying Marvell stock rests on the staggering acceleration of its addressable market and management's aggressive yet highly credible multi-year financial targets. At its recent Investor Day event, Marvell's management laid out a massive long-term growth strategy driven by artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure demand. Marvell also raised its near-term growth projection, signaling accelerating growth.

More News from Barchart

Elon Musk Sets the Record Straight on Terafab. What It Means for Intel, TSMC, and SpaceX Stocks.

Why Super Micro Stock Is Heading to $60

A $1.3 Billion Reason Why IONQ Stock Is Down Today

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

As spending on data centers and AI technology continues to increase, Marvell stands to benefit from stronger demand for its products and solutions. Its top and bottom lines are expected to grow rapidly, giving MRVL stock a solid boost.

Marvell Set to Deliver Substantial Growth

Marvell appears well-positioned to capitalize on the expanding AI infrastructure market and sustain strong growth through the end of the decade. The company's decision to increase its revenue outlook highlights stronger demand for AI-related technologies and improving opportunities across the broader semiconductor industry.

In the near term, management expects revenue to reach about $20 billion in fiscal 2028, $2 billion higher than its previous forecast and around 67% YOY. Overall, Marvell projects its revenue to increase at a CAGR of 55% to 60% through fiscal 2031.

The data center segment is expected to remain a major contributor to Marvell's growth, supported by demand across multiple AI infrastructure applications. Management anticipates that data center revenue will increase at a CAGR of 65% between fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2031, highlighting the strong demand expected over the next several years.

Rising capital expenditures by hyperscale cloud providers are providing a significant tailwind. Marvell's presence in several essential AI infrastructure markets, including high-speed optical connectivity, networking and switching, and custom silicon, positions the company to benefit from continued investment in AI computing capacity.

Story Continues

Within data centers, interconnect is expected to be a key growth driver. Demand for 800G optical products remains strong, while newer 1.6T solutions could contribute more to revenue starting in fiscal 2028. Marvell expects its interconnect business to grow at a 65% CAGR through fiscal 2031. Its switching and storage businesses are also expected to expand, with revenue projected to grow at a 45% CAGR over the same period.

Custom silicon offers another significant growth opportunity. Marvell expects this business to grow at an 80% CAGR through fiscal 2031, with revenue projected to more than triple in fiscal 2029 compared with fiscal 2028. As demand for custom chips increases, this segment could become an increasingly important contributor to the company's overall growth and profitability.

Marvell's expanding custom silicon business and improving operating efficiency could drive significant earnings growth in the coming years. Management expects profits to grow faster than revenue, with EPS potentially surpassing $30 by fiscal 2031. In the near term, analysts forecast MRVL's EPS to rise to $5.99 in fiscal 2028. This indicates that Marvell's EPS will likely grow at a solid pace between fiscal 2028 and fiscal 2031.

Time to Load Up on Marvell Stock

Marvell's accelerating growth outlook, expanding custom silicon business, and strong exposure to AI data center infrastructure provide a compelling case for buying the stock. Management's improved revenue outlook and projected annual revenue growth of 55%–60% through fiscal 2031 point to significant expansion opportunities. Meanwhile, better operating efficiency could help earnings grow even faster than revenue.

While the stock's recent rally raises valuation concerns, continued investment in AI infrastructure and rising demand for high-speed connectivity and custom semiconductors could drive further upside.

Wall Street analysts remain optimistic about Marvell, with the stock carrying a "Strong Buy" consensus rating. The highest price target of $450 suggests about 63% upside from its recent close of $275.28.

news.Title: Elon Musk explains why chip stocks are getting drilled on news out of China
news.Content:
Hot chip stocks like Micron ( MU ) and Sandisk ( SNDK ) are taking it on the chin out of the gate this week.

Ask the world's richest person, Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, and he will probably say the sell-off is just beginning.

"When China figures out how to manufacture a product, their ability to scale is often greater than the rest of the world combined. We saw this with lithium batteries and solar, for example," Musk said in a new post on X .

Musk was replying to a post about the fresh chip stock sell-off, which is being fueled by Chinese tech player CXMT . The company's president, Cao Kanyu, called out "key progress" on a new cell architecture at an event in Shanghai over the weekend.

CXMT plans to roll out new memory products based on the architecture by the end of the year.

The development sparked concern that growing Chinese competition could threaten memory chip pricing power, causing investors to unwind crowded momentum AI trades.

Micron shed 3.8% in Monday's trading session and is down another 4% in premarket trading today. Sandisk lost 5.9% on Monday and is off by 5% today.

Sharp sell-offs are also being seen in other memory names, including SK Hynix ( SKHY ), Western Digital ( WDC ), and Seagate ( STX ).

Added Musk, "SpaceX is a rare counter-example, where its mass to orbit is roughly an order of magnitude greater than the rest of the world, BUT China now does the majority of non-SpaceX mass to orbit. SpaceX is an anomaly in the matrix. Maybe RAM will be different, but RAM was a low margin commodity only ~3 years ago. LP5 and LP6 are designed to a common standard that China seems to be solving fast."

news.Title: Is Western Digital (WDC) a Good or Bad Investment at Today’s Price?
news.Content:
Western Digital Corporation (NASDAQ: WDC ) closed at $397.28 on October 9. The stock has returned 13.4% during the last six months, compared to a 24.3% return for the Insider Monkey Billionaire Index and 15.1% for State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust.

Western Digital reports a net margin no hardware manufacturer has ever sustained. Storage has a long history of destroying anyone who mistakes a shortage for a moat. This is a shortage.

READ ALSO: 10 Best Undervalued Stocks to Buy in October

The Profit Came From a Shareholding, Not From Drives:

No storage company keeps nearly three-quarters of its revenue as profit, and this one did not either. Western Digital separated its flash memory business as SanDisk in February 2025 and retained a stake. Accounting rules require that retained interest be marked to market, and SanDisk shares rose a long way. The resulting gain is most of the reported profit.

The cash statement confirms it plainly. Free cash flow came in at a fraction of reported net income, and that spread is the shareholding rather than the drives. Strip it out and what remains is genuinely strong, because the operating margin of 43.61% belongs to Western Digital and it is a remarkable number for storage hardware. Revenue grew 43.80% as data centres bought high-capacity drives faster than the industry could build them, on a balance sheet carrying barely a billion of debt. The stake itself is in a chip business, which is the sector doing the work here and the reason so much money sits in the semiconductors billionaires added to this year . Their most-held name is up 18% since June.

DON'T MISS: 10 Best Stocks to Buy for High Returns in 2026

This Is What a Cycle Top Looks Like:

Storage is cyclical, and this is what the top of a cycle looks like. Drive prices rose because buyers wanted capacity faster than it could be manufactured, not because Western Digital won share.

That matters for how the multiple should be read. A cyclical trades at its lowest earnings multiple precisely when its earnings are highest, which is the opposite of a bargain signal. Micron spent years looking cheap on exactly this arithmetic and expensive once memory pricing turned.

Capacity is already being added across the industry, which is the predictable response to margins like these. The question is not whether supply arrives but when. Cheapest multiple at the highest earnings is the oldest trap in commodities, and avoiding it is most of what separates a cyclical from the high return list we published in January . The one we ranked first there is up 24% since.

Story Continues

The shares rose over six months without keeping pace with the market, and they still sit far below their 52-week high, which gives some sense of how violent the swings here are.

The Valuation Case:

On earnings, the stock trades at 12.40 times forward, on analyst consensus estimates, and that figure is not a bargain signal for the reasons above. The price-to-book of 18.99 is the measure that does not flatter the company, and it is the one that survives a pricing reversal. You are paying nineteen times the stated value of the assets for a manufacturer at a cyclical peak.

The verdict is that Western Digital looks cheap on peak earnings and expensive on assets, which is the classic profile of a cyclical at the top. Both things are true, and only one of them persists through a downturn. The operating business deserves credit, and the price does not reflect a permanent rerating. Profit that does not depend on a shortage is a different kind of cheap altogether, and that is what the profitable stocks we judged most underpriced are built on. Their leader has returned 16% since.

Conclusion:

Two businesses are buried in this income statement, and only one of them makes drives. The one that does grew revenue sharply at an exceptional operating margin, on a balance sheet carrying almost no debt. However, the net margin comes mostly from marking a retained SanDisk shareholding, and free cash flow arrived well below reported net income. The forward multiple is what a storage company looks like at the top of a pricing cycle rather than what a cheap one looks like. Everything comes back to price-to-book, the one figure that does not fall away when drive prices do.

Market Sentiment:

Western Digital Corporation (NASDAQ:WDC) was held by 98 hedge funds with a combined stake value of about $9.94 billion at the end of Q2 2026 in the Insider Monkey database. This is up from 83 hedge fund holders with a cumulative investment value of around $6.57 billion in the previous quarter.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of WDC as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than WDC and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock .

news.Title: S&P upgrades SanDisk to BBB as AI memory demand drives cash flow past $23B
news.Content:
Investing.com -- S&P Global Ratings upgraded SanDisk Corporation (NASDAQ:SNDK). to 'BBB' from 'BB+' on Monday, citing a sharp surge in artificial intelligence-driven demand for memory chips and a pristine, debt-free balance sheet. The credit rating agency maintained a stable outlook for the NAND flash memory producer, highlighting robust cash generation and significant financial cushion to absorb potential industry downturns.

The upgrade follows a transformative period of growth for SanDisk, driven by a tight supply-demand imbalance in the global flash memory market. Fueled by exponential growth in AI data center infrastructure, the company posted a 175% revenue surge in fiscal 2026 as pricing skyrocketed across all business segments.

Not finding the right stocks? Our AI's list of investor-grade stock picks for October just dropped »

Looking ahead, S&P expects SanDisk's momentum to accelerate into fiscal 2027, projecting revenue to double and free cash flow to surpass $23 billion. Operating profitability is anticipated to expand further as the company ramps up lower-cost technology and benefits from high-margin data center contracts featuring volume commitments and price protections.

While memory markets remain historically cyclical and prone to sudden price corrections, SanDisk's conservative balance sheet structure provides substantial risk mitigation. The company repaid all of its funded debt earlier in the year and is expected to maintain a net cash position even as capital expenditures increase and excess capital is returned to shareholders.

Against that backdrop, long-term supply agreement commitments from data center customers are providing enhanced earnings visibility compared to traditional PC and mobile markets. S&P noted that while new supply capacity from competitors could emerge by 2028, SanDisk's balance sheet retains ample strength to navigate future market shifts.

news.Title: AI Is Blowing Up Tech’s Money Rules. How Arm Could Make Qualcomm Pay More.
news.Content:
Artificial intelligence is doing more than changing what technology companies sell. It is testing the agreements that decide who gets paid when those products succeed. A licensing deal that looked sensible in the smartphone era can look painfully cheap once the same technology powers sprawling data centers. Meanwhile, content once given away to attract readers has become raw material for competing AI services.

Investors riding the AI infrastructure spending boom should take note: owning essential technology doesn't guarantee a bigger share of its value.

More News from Barchart

'When You Say I Should Pay $100 Billion, Then I'm Starting To Do A Little Math': Bill Gates Said He'd Happily Pay 'Over $10 Billion In Taxes' But Some Are Asking Too Much

Dan Ives Calls SpaceX's $40B Nvidia Chip Debt Plan a 'Smart Move'

Dear Johnson & Johnson Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for October 13

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

Qualcomm and Arm's $1.88 Problem

That tension is on full display in the courtroom fight between Qualcomm (QCOM) and Arm Holdings (ARM) over an architecture licensing agreement dating to 2013. Oddly, Arm is now criticizing the very terms it wrote.

According to Reuters , the agreement caps royalties at $1.88 per chip containing at least five processor cores. Arm's lawyer contrasted that with data center processors containing 288 cores, asking whether Qualcomm was paying for five and "getting 283 for free." Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon rejected that characterization.

The stakes cut both ways. For Qualcomm, a capped fee protects margins as its chips grow more capable. For Arm, it limits the revenue it can capture from that growing complexity. And because Qualcomm's license runs through 2033, access to future technology, and what it costs, is central to the dispute.

Arm has another route to monetization, though. Its June-quarter SEC filing describes the March 2026 launch of its own AGI CPU, underscoring a shift from licensing toward selling silicon.

A little arithmetic shows why this matters. On a hypothetical $100 chip, a $1.88 royalty is 1.88% of sales. On a $1,000 chip, it shrinks to 0.188%. These are illustrations, not Qualcomm's actual prices, but they show how a fixed fee lets a chipmaker keep more revenue as product value rises. A pricier chip also costs more to design and build, so the difference isn't pure profit.

Still, the distinction is useful. Arm shareholders should separate more chips shipped from more revenue earned per chip. Qualcomm shareholders face the opposite question: how much of today's cost advantage will survive negotiations over tomorrow's technology?

Story Continues

AI Is Repricing Content Too

A similar reset is underway online. Reddit (RDDT) disclosed in its 2024 IPO prospectus that its January data-licensing agreements totaled $203 million over two to three years. That figure is the contracted value, not cash already collected. Because these contracts are shorter than Arm's, Reddit gets more frequent chances to revisit pricing.

Charging AI companies has its own trade-off, however. Their answers can reduce the need to visit the original source, and Reddit's slowing user growth shows that monetizing content and protecting audience engagement are separate challenges.

Microsoft (MSFT) took a different approach on Feb. 3 with its Publisher Content Marketplace, which lets publishers set licensing terms and provides usage reporting. The announcement explicitly acknowledged that the web's old bargain of content in exchange for referral traffic doesn't translate cleanly to AI.

Key Takeaway

As for the Qualcomm-Arm case, Reuters reports that the Delaware jury deliberated for roughly four hours on Oct. 9 without reaching a verdict and plans to return on Oct. 13. But the tension over these contracts will remain whichever way the jury decides.

AI demand alone is an incomplete investment thesis. The better bets are businesses that can turn rising usage into cash without undermining customer relationships or their original source of revenue.

For now, keep QCOM and ARM stocks on your watchlist rather than buying either on courtroom speculation. Watch for the verdict, future licensing terms, and evidence that Arm's silicon expansion produces profitable growth. Arm's $1.88 fee illustrates the problem, but it is enforceable pricing power that determines who collects the payoff.

news.Title: Not Sandisk, Not Intel. This Stock Will Lead the S&P 500 Next Year
news.Content:
The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) has had a great year so far. The average annual return of the S&P 500 is about 10%, and with it sitting at about 14.5% right now, it has been a good year. There are still a few months left, so the chances of it ending up even higher are quite good.

While the S&P 500 as a whole is doing well, a few individual performers stand out. Sandisk holds the title for best-performing S&P 500 stock this year, rising about 590% in 2026. Intel is another top performer, increasing nearly 200% so far this year. There are a handful of companies that also have had strong runs, including AMD .

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

So, which stock will lead the S&P 500 higher next year? I think it will be a familiar face, and it won't be one of these three.

Some stocks have gotten ahead of themselves

With the returns some stocks are delivering this year, it's pretty easy to guess that next year may not be as kind to these stocks. Many companies have far outgrown their business results and are trading at inflated valuations, such as Intel and AMD. These two trade for 70 and 81 times forward earnings, respectively. This showcases just how expensive they are. Others, like Sandisk, operate in a cyclical market, and the stock market is wary of giving it a standard valuation due to fears of the memory chip industry seeing a cyclical downturn.

Regardless, there are a handful of stocks that were abandoned to pave the way for these to rise, and the most obvious one is Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA). Nvidia led the S&P 500 in performance during 2023 and 2024, and I think it has a strong shot at leading it again in 2027. Why? Its stock has been ignored compared to some of its peers.

Nvidia is dirt cheap compared to its peers

It's hard to say that the largest company in the world by market cap isn't getting a fair shake, but that's exactly what's happening. As mentioned above, AMD trades at over 80 times forward earnings. Nvidia trades at 25.

AMD PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

These two companies operate in the same industry (namely, graphics processing units , or GPUs), and Nvidia is growing its data center business (the segment most exposed to artificial intelligence (AI)) at a faster pace. In Q2, Nvidia's data center division grew at a 117% pace to $89 billion. AMD's data center division grew at a 107% pace to $6.7 billion. Nvidia is still winning, and there's no reason to give AMD a ridiculous premium as a result.

Story Continues

Another factor is that the market hasn't priced in practically any of 2027's growth into Nvidia's stock price. The S&P 500 trades for about 20 times forward earnings. The slight premium Nvidia now commands is worth it given its positioning in the AI boom and strong track record of performance. However, Nvidia is also expected to grow its revenue by 70% next year. But Nvidia's current 25 times forward earnings valuation implies that its stock will grow at a market-average pace next year (about 10%).

That's a major mismatch, and I think it suggests Nvidia is poised for an exceptional year and could lead the S&P 500 in performance. While there could be others that sneak up on investors and outperform Nvidia, Nvidia is one of the few companies that has given investors high visibility into its future growth. Management has undergirded nearly every step along the way, so this 70% growth could also be a major undershoot.

With Nvidia expected to grow revenue by 70% or more next year, I think it's a no-brainer buy right now.

news.Title: Prediction: Sandisk Stock Will Be Worth This Much at the End of 2026
news.Content:
Since spinning off from Western Digital in February 2025, Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) has become one of the biggest beneficiaries of the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure boom. Over the past year, Sandisk stock has soared 1,100%. In 2026 alone, its gain of 570% makes it the second best performer in the Nasdaq-100 .

Yet despite its extraordinary price appreciation, Sandisk trades at a modest valuation. With memory shortages potentially extending through 2028, could Sandisk's valuation actually be too conservative?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

How the memory shortage is benefiting Sandisk

Sandisk specializes in NAND flash memory, a technology used to power solid-state drives, smartphones, computers, and storage systems. While Nvidia GPUs receive most of the attention surrounding AI chips, the enormous amounts of data generated by those accelerators must be stored somewhere. That's creating a powerful tailwind for storage suppliers.

During its late September earnings report, Micron Technology indicated that memory supply bottlenecks could persist through 2027 and 2028. This commentary aligns with Sandisk's management, which has previously highlighted how strong customer demand is limiting supply.

So far, the memory boom has made a dramatic financial impact on Sandisk. The company generated $20.3 billion in revenue during fiscal 2026, representing 175% year-over-year growth. Meanwhile, Wall Street expects fiscal 2027 revenue to approach $49 billion, more than doubling again. For a historically cyclical industry, these are encouraging growth numbers.

Sandisk's valuation still has room to expand

Wall Street expects Sandisk to generate approximately $215 in earnings per share during fiscal 2027. At a share price around $1,585, that translates into a forward price-to-earnings ratio of just 7.4. That looks inexpensive given the company's explosive revenue and profit growth.

SNDK Revenue (TTM) data by YCharts

It's important to note that memory manufacturers have historically traded at lower multiples because their profitability is more sensitive to supply and demand dynamics. When memory prices fall, earnings can erode surprisingly quickly.

But what if this AI-driven cycle is different? If AI infrastructure demand continues accelerating while NAND production remains constrained, Sandisk should enjoy unusually strong earnings for several years. This is what makes the company's shift toward multi-year customer agreements so savvy, as they provide more predictable revenue and earnings potential. In turn, growth investors could begin to assign Sandisk stock a higher valuation multiple.

Story Continues

Where could Sandisk stock trade by December?

In a downside scenario, investors may become concerned about weakening NAND prices or an eventual supply glut. If Sandisk were to trade at 5.5 times projected earnings, shares could retreat toward $1,182, representing about 25% downside to today's prices.

What I think is most realistic is Micron's supply outlook will prove accurate following Sandisk's upcoming earnings report on Oct. 29. At that time, investors could become more comfortable expanding the multiple. At nine times forward earnings, Sandisk would trade at approximately $1,935, implying 22% upside.

In a particularly bullish scenario, Sandisk's guidance could trigger both upward earnings revisions and multiple expansion. At 11 times projected earnings, Sandisk could approach $2,365, representing roughly 49% upside.

All told, I see a reasonable path toward $1,900 by year's end. Smart investors understand that Sandisk's modest valuation profile could reflect peak-cycle earnings rather than a genuine bargain. Nevertheless, secular tailwinds suggest Sandisk will continue benefiting from AI infrastructure demand and constrained memory supply. Against this backdrop, Sandisk looks like a compelling semiconductor stock to buy and hold as AI infrastructure continues to accelerate.

news.Title: Teradyne Boosts Test Portfolio With Titan HP: Can It Beat KLAC & COHU?
news.Content:
Teradyne TER is benefiting from robust demand for advanced semiconductor testing solutions, driven by accelerating AI data center investments, increasing chip complexity, and growing requirements for high-performance computing infrastructure. The company's expanding test portfolio, particularly its latest Titan HP platform enhancements, strengthens its competitive position against KLA KLAC and Cohu COHU, which are also capitalizing on AI-driven semiconductor investments.

Teradyne recently introduced enhanced burn-in capabilities for its Titan HP platform, targeting high-power AI data center devices, automotive chips and other high-reliability semiconductors. The production-ready platform integrates reliability stress testing with system-level testing, enabling precise per-device thermal control under realistic workloads. Its asynchronous slot architecture allows independent testing, improving efficiency and reducing equipment downtime. Powered by Teradyne's Atlas software, Titan HP enables manufacturers to streamline testing, reduce capital costs, optimize factory floor space and accelerate time to market. The platform is already deployed in production, strengthening Teradyne's semiconductor testing portfolio across the AI device supply chain.

Teradyne's strengthening position in AI-driven semiconductor testing is noteworthy. In the second quarter of 2026, Semi Test revenues surged 128% year over year, while compute revenues jumped nearly 600%, reflecting strong AI-related demand. The growing adoption of advanced packaging, AI accelerators and high-bandwidth memory is expected to drive demand for increasingly advanced testing solutions.

Teradyne's robust AI test portfolio and strong customer traction are likely to strengthen its competitive position against KLA and Cohu. For the third quarter of 2026, Teradyne expects revenues in the range of $1.20-$1.30 billion.

news.Title: Semtech Rises 154% YTD: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
Semtech Corporation SMTC shares have surged 154.1% year to date (YTD), outperforming the Zacks Semiconductor - Analog and Mixed industry's growth of 45.2%. The stock also outperformed its industry peers, including Microchip Technology MCHP, ON Semiconductor ON and NXP Semiconductors NXPI. YTD, shares of Microchip Technology, ON Semiconductor and NXP Semiconductors have gained 18.6%, 43.1% and 4.8%, respectively.

The outperformance of SMTC's shares raises the question: Does it still have room to run, or is it time for investors to consider taking profits? Let's find out.

YTD Price Return Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Semtech's 1.6T Ramp to Drive Data Center Growth

Semtech is seeing strong demand for its data center products as hyperscalers increase spending on AI infrastructure. The company's data center revenues reached a record $100 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 39% sequentially and 91% year over year. Growth was driven by continued strength in 800G products, along with the ramp of 1.6T CopperEdge and FiberEdge solutions. Management expects this momentum to continue, with data center revenues projected to increase 45% sequentially and 160% year over year in the third quarter of fiscal 2027.

The 1.6T transition could become an important growth driver for Semtech. Management expects 1.6T FiberEdge and CopperEdge products to account for more than 50% of total data center revenues in the third quarter of fiscal 2027. Semtech is also gaining market share in optical connectivity, where its FiberEdge business has grown from about 18% market share in 800G two years ago to more than 50%. Further, the company expects its 1.6T FiberEdge market share to exceed 50% by the end of fiscal 2027.

The company is also preparing for the next stage of data center growth. Semtech is expanding its photonics portfolio through gain chips, high-power CW lasers, semiconductor optical amplifiers and photodiodes. These products are aimed at higher-speed applications, including 3.2T transceivers and co-packaged optics. Management expects its content per transceiver to increase from high single-digit dollars to high double-digit dollars as data center speeds move from 800G to 3.2T.

Strong customer demand supports SMTC's prospects as well, with the company reporting that its backlog for the remainder of fiscal 2027 was fully booked and more than 70% of its target for fiscal 2028 was already covered. Management is also working with manufacturing partners to secure additional capacity for fiscal 2028 and beyond. If it can meet customer requirements and maintain its product momentum, the 1.6T ramp could remain an important driver of Semtech's data center growth over the next several quarters.

Story Continues

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for SMTC's fiscal 2027 and 2028 revenues indicates year-over-year growth of 41.5% and 28.5%, respectively.

Strong LoRa Growth Boosts SMTC's Prospects

Semtech is seeing strong growth in its LoRa business as demand increases across industrial, commercial and consumer applications. LoRa-enabled net sales reached a record $58 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 31% sequentially and 58% year over year. Growth reflects wider adoption of LoRa across different applications, including smart homes, security systems and industrial monitoring. Management expects the business to maintain its momentum, with LoRa revenues projected to grow about 15% sequentially and 65% year over year in the third quarter of fiscal 2027.

Semtech is expanding its LoRa portfolio to address more applications. Its LoRa Gen 4 platform supports higher data speeds while maintaining low power consumption and long-range connectivity. These features can support new uses in smart homes, security and industrial applications. For example, LoRa-enabled sensors can help monitor industrial equipment and support predictive maintenance. In public safety, the technology can also enable sensors to transmit audio for AI-based verification instead of sending simple alerts.

Amazon Sidewalk is another potential growth driver for Semtech's LoRa business. Following Ring's launch of a new range of LoRa-based sensors in the United States, Amazon Sidewalk is expanding internationally, starting with Canada and Mexico, while Europe, Australia and Japan are expected to follow. This expansion could help increase the use of LoRa-based devices in consumer applications through Amazon's network. Meanwhile, LoRa Plus is gaining traction in smart home and security markets, broadening the company's opportunities beyond traditional industrial and commercial use cases.

Strong momentum in LoRaWAN, LoRa Plus and Amazon Sidewalk can also support SMTC's future growth. Management expects LoRa revenues to grow at a rate above its previous 20% benchmark, supported by demand across these applications. With record revenues, new use cases and expanding distribution through Amazon Sidewalk, LoRa could become an increasingly important contributor to Semtech's overall growth.

SMTC's Valuation Reflects High Growth Expectations

SMTC is currently trading at a higher price-to-sales (P/S) multiple compared with the industry. SMTC's forward 12-month P/S ratio sits at 9.82X, higher than the industry's forward 12-month P/S ratio of 8.43X.

SMTC Forward 12-Month P/S Ratio

SMTC stock also trades at a higher P/S multiple compared with other industry peers, including Microchip Technology, ON Semiconductor and NXP Semiconductors. At present, Microchip Technology, ON Semiconductor and NXP Semiconductors have P/S multiples of 5.89X, 4.18X and 3.72X, respectively.

SMTC's rally reflects investor excitement about AI-related data center demand, putting it above industry and peers in terms of valuation, reflecting the high growth expectations of the company in the long term.

Conclusion: Buy SMTC Stock Right Now

Semtech is seeing strong demand for AI data center products, with the ramp-up of 1.6T solutions driving revenue growth and a strong backlog supporting future demand. The company's LoRa business is growing as adoption increases across smart homes, security and industrial applications. These factors support the outlook for continued growth. Further, the stock's valuation reflects high growth expectations, which are set to benefit from rising AI data center spending and wider adoption of LoRa technology.

news.Title: Brokers Suggest Investing in Lam Research (LRCX): Read This Before Placing a Bet
news.Content:
The recommendations of Wall Street analysts are often relied on by investors when deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock. Media reports about these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts changing their ratings often affect a stock's price. Do they really matter, though?

Let's take a look at what these Wall Street heavyweights have to say about Lam Research (LRCX) before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage.

Lam Research currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.51, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 34 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.51 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 34 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 23 are Strong Buy and four are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 67.7% and 11.8% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for LRCX

Check price target & stock forecast for Lam Research here>>>

While the ABR calls for buying Lam Research, it may not be wise to make an investment decision solely based on this information. Several studies have shown limited to no success of brokerage recommendations in guiding investors to pick stocks with the best price increase potential.

Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations.

In other words, their interests aren't always aligned with retail investors, rarely indicating where the price of a stock could actually be heading. Therefore, the best use of this information could be validating your own research or an indicator that has proven to be highly successful in predicting a stock's price movement.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, which classifies stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), is a reliable indicator of a stock's near-term price performance. So, validating the Zacks Rank with ABR could go a long way in making a profitable investment decision.

Zacks Rank Should Not Be Confused With ABR

Although both Zacks Rank and ABR are displayed in a range of 1--5, they are different measures altogether.

Broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

Story Continues

Analysts employed by brokerage firms have been and continue to be overly optimistic with their recommendations. Since the ratings issued by these analysts are more favorable than their research would support because of the vested interest of their employers, they mislead investors far more often than they guide.

In contrast, the Zacks Rank is driven by earnings estimate revisions. And near-term stock price movements are strongly correlated with trends in earnings estimate revisions, according to empirical research.

In addition, the different Zacks Rank grades are applied proportionately to all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide current-year earnings estimates. In other words, this tool always maintains a balance among its five ranks.

Another key difference between the ABR and Zacks Rank is freshness. The ABR is not necessarily up-to-date when you look at it. But, since brokerage analysts keep revising their earnings estimates to account for a company's changing business trends, and their actions get reflected in the Zacks Rank quickly enough, it is always timely in indicating future price movements.

Is LRCX Worth Investing In?

In terms of earnings estimate revisions for Lam Research, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 0.2% over the past month to $9.34.

Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to soar in the near term.

The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for Lam Research. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>>

Therefore, the Buy-equivalent ABR for Lam Research may serve as a useful guide for investors.

news.Title: 3 Tech Stocks Wall Street Upgraded Last Week, and the One I'd Buy First
news.Content:
Three tech stocks got Wall Street upgrades last week: Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), Palantir (NASDAQ: PLTR), and Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL). Marvell has climbed 224% year to date, while Palantir is up 17% and Microsoft has trailed the S&P 500 's 14% gain.

All three have solid catalysts and could be solid long-term investments, but Marvell offers the best growth for the price.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Microsoft

On Oct. 5, Melius Research analyst Ben Reitzes upgraded Microsoft from hold to buy with a $665 price target. That implies about 25% upside from the current share price.

With growing concerns around AI safety, the analyst sees Microsoft's cybersecurity offerings benefiting from the adoption of AI agents. On the company's fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call in July, CEO Satya Nadella highlighted the advantages of Agent 365. It extends security tools to AI agents, and nearly 40 million agents are already registered on the platform, reflecting the advantage Microsoft has from its long-running relationships with leading enterprises.

Azure, the cloud backbone for Microsoft's AI services, continues to benefit from surging demand. Revenue from Azure and other cloud services grew 43% year over year in fiscal Q4 2026, which ended in June, and management said demand still exceeds capacity.

The stock trades at 27 times forward earnings, based on fiscal 2027 estimates. The consensus analyst estimate is for earnings to grow at an annualized rate of 15% in the coming years. That's a reasonable price-to-earnings-to-growth (PEG) multiple of 1.8x.

The main risk is that growth depends on how quickly Microsoft can add data center capacity, a process that requires heavy spending and could drag on margins and earnings. Still, a slightly higher P/E and continued growth in the business put the $665 price target within realistic reach over the next year, with more gains in store for investors who hold for the long term.

Palantir Technologies

On Oct. 8, Goldman Sachs analyst Gabriela Borges upgraded Palantir from neutral to buy with a $230 price target. That implies about 10% upside from the current share price.

Palantir shares have surged about 65% in the last three months, but the analyst sees further upside as companies seek to control their own data and AI models. That should increase demand for Palantir's custom-built applications with each enterprise customer.

Story Continues

This builds on the trends Palantir is already seeing. Palantir's Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) lets companies build and run AI models using their proprietary data. That is one of the main factors that appeals to prospective customers who want full control over their data and don't want it used to train another company's AI models.

Management's full-year 2026 guidance calls for revenue of approximately $8.1 billion, up about 82% from 2025. Analysts expect 53% annualized earnings growth in the coming years. However, it trades at a forward earnings multiple of 123 -- a PEG multiple of 2.3x. I hold Palantir in my portfolio, but I don't expect it to hit the analyst's price target in the near term. Marvell offers a better valuation relative to expected growth.

Marvell Technology

If I were adding new money to any of the three right now, it would be Marvell. On Oct. 7, TD Cowen analyst Sean O'Loughlin upgraded Marvell from hold to buy with a $350 price target. That implies about 27% upside from the current share price.

The upgrade follows Marvell's Investor Day on Oct. 6, 2026, where management highlighted the momentum in its connectivity business -- the chips and optics that move data inside AI data centers. O'Loughlin sees the risk around its custom chip business fading. These risks centered on the low margins custom chips produce and Marvell's dependence on selling these chips to a few customers.

During the investor day conference, CEO Matt Murphy raised the company's fiscal 2028 revenue outlook to about $20 billion. He said the shift from AI training to inference and the use of agents will drive greater demand for connectivity equipment, with optics already accelerating, backing up the analyst's thesis.

Marvell is also positioned to capture a growing share of AI infrastructure spending with its custom silicon business. These are chips designed for specific tasks, such as cloud giants' AI workloads. That business is expected to grow from $1.5 billion in revenue in 2025 to $12 billion by fiscal 2029.

The stock trades at 65 times 2027 earnings estimates, with analysts expecting 49% annualized earnings growth in the next several years. Marvell offers the lowest PEG ratio of the three at 1.3x. This could support the stock reaching the analyst's price target over the next year, while also setting up the potential for excellent returns for an investor who buys today and holds for the long term.

news.Title: Elon Musk just handed Intel a new problem Wall Street can't ignore
news.Content: Few deals have done more for Intel's story this year than its seat at Elon Musk's chip table. Intel joined the Terafab project on April 7. It was the first major outside commitment for a foundry business that had only ever made chips for itself. The stock more than doubled that month, its best on record. Musk also confirmed on Tesla's first-quarter earnings call that Terafab will use Intel's 14A process. Now Musk has invited a far bigger name into the conversation. In a post on X , he confirmed that Terafab is in talks with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing. He called them early discussions, but said something may come of them. Also read: Elon Musk delivers 6-word warning on future of employment What Musk actually confirmed The talks first surfaced in Tim Culpan's Culpium newsletter. TSMC has not commented publicly. One possibility is that TSMC would build and run a plant serving only Tesla, SpaceX and xAI. The ownership setup is far from settled. That is what makes the news uncomfortable for Intel. Intel is the only other named partner and is reportedly supplying its 14A manufacturing process for Terafab's chips. If TSMC joins, Intel's process could be dropped in favor of TSMC's own technology, according to CNBC . Intel does hold a cross-patent license with TSMC that Terafab lacks, which could complicate any use of an Intel-developed process. Intel is not walking away. Chief Executive Lip-Bu Tan said the company will keep working with Musk on Terafab, according to Reuters . Speculation about a TSMC partnership had worried investors. TSMC also has its own American expansion underway. It is reportedly weighing several new chip plants in Texas, each costing at least $20 billion. That is on top of an existing plan to invest $265 billion in the U.S. TSMC also dominates the market for advanced chip packaging. Why Musk needs so many chips Terafab is not a small side project. Tesla, SpaceX and xAI launched it in Austin on March 21 as a joint venture to make AI chips near Giga Texas. The goal is to combine logic, memory and advanced packaging in one place, cutting reliance on suppliers such as TSMC and Samsung. Tesla's AI5 chip is among the first products it is designed to make. Musk frames it as a matter of survival. "We either build the Terafab, or we don't have the chips," he said. He added that every existing fab on Earth produces only about 2% of what Tesla and SpaceX will eventually need. His big announcements have often come with overly ambitious timelines. The plan calls for two kinds of chips. One would run self-driving software and Optimus robots. A version hardened for the space environment would power the orbital data centers SpaceX wants to build. The ultimate goal is a terawatt of computing capacity a year. Story Continues The targets behind that demand are huge. SpaceX plans to launch orbital data centers within a couple of years. Tesla wants to build 1 million Optimus robots a year within five years, as reported by The Motley Fool . Tesla also sees room to grow car production as its robotaxi service expands. Neither TSMC nor Intel can supply that much on its own today. Intel's foundry still needs outside customers The foundry business is growing, at least on paper. Intel Foundry brought in $5.8 billion in the second quarter, up 31% year over year. Its operating loss also narrowed. Most of that money comes from Intel itself. External foundry revenue was only $293 million in the quarter. The 14A process is progressing faster than the previous node did at the same stage. Risk production is targeted for 2027, according to Nasdaq . Intel's total revenue rose 25% to about $16.1 billion, well ahead of forecasts. More Intel: Meta Muse gives AMD and Intel investors a reason to cheer Intel's $20 billion stock sale has surprising upside Nvidia just sent a strong signal to AMD and Intel investors That is the gap Wall Street keeps pointing to. Mizuho analyst Vijay Rakesh sees advanced-packaging revenue reaching about $3.5 billion by 2029 as 14A gains traction. The absence of outside customer commitments for Intel's current 18A process has weighed on the stock. Building that business is expensive. In August, Intel announced a $15 billion stock offering, possibly its first public equity sale since it listed in 1971. It also raised its 2026 capital spending plan above $20 billion. What it means for Intel shareholders The stock has already priced in a lot of hope. Intel hit an all-time high near $142 in late June, its first record since August 2000. A preliminary chipmaking deal with Apple helped drive that move. Related: AT&T CEO holds firm stance on Elon Musk's SpaceX phone strategy It has been a bumpy ride since. Intel traded around $96 in early September, roughly 32% below its June peak. Mizuho cut its price target to $92 while keeping a hold rating. Rakesh still sees a chance that server processor supply stays tight through 2027. Valuation leaves little room for disappointment. The shares have surged sharply since early April. A threat to one of its biggest catalysts would make that price harder to justify. Intel could still lead Terafab's manufacturing with TSMC in a supporting role. But Musk's confirmation shows that the deal is no longer Intel's alone. news.Title: The Best Stock to Invest $10,000 In Right Now
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) could be a perfect opportunity to buy with $10,000. While the stock has tripled in 52 weeks, it's also down 20% from its 2026 high. Many investors see the pullback as a chance to add to their position.

Indeed, behind the sell-off are major developments that could make Marvell's AI story more attractive than it appears today, such as its custom silicon business, which could become one of its biggest growth drivers.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Custom silicon could become a much bigger growth engine

Marvell just delivered another record quarter, with revenue accelerating 37% year over year and data center revenue growing 46%. Management said AI-related bookings remain exceptionally strong and raised its revenue outlook for both fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028.

AI demand is clearly a key driver of Marvell's business, with its data center business now accounting for around four-fifths of revenue, giving Marvell much greater exposure to the AI build-out. So it should be no surprise that Marvell is becoming a key supplier of custom silicon for hyperscalers.

A perfect example of this is Marvell's expanded relationship with Alphabet , for example, which covers a broad range of custom products connected to Google's Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) ecosystem, including AI chips, storage and networking hardware, and memory interface products.

Marvell is also working on 18 custom AI chip projects for four major hyperscalers and several fast-growing AI companies. That includes both AI chips and the supporting devices needed to connect and power them.

Management also said that its Custom business should accelerate in the second half of fiscal 2027. That gives investors a major growth engine just as the company's existing data center connectivity business picks up.

That shows the breadth of opportunity. Marvell isn't simply betting on one piece of the AI stack. It's also building out the connectivity layer that allows all this AI compute to work together.

Optical connectivity gives Marvell another growth catalyst

Perhaps one of the most exciting parts of Marvell's strategy is its push into optical connectivity. The company completed its acquisition of Celestial AI to add Photonic Fabric technology, which is designed to provide high-bandwidth, high-speed connections across large-scale AI systems.

Story Continues

That matters because AI systems are becoming more distributed. As clusters grow, moving information between chips becomes just as important as the chips themselves. Marvell is positioning itself to benefit from that trend by supplying hardware that facilitates the flow of information between these chips.

Celestial AI also gives Marvell exposure to a new market rather than simply adding another product to an existing one. Marvell sees the technology as opening up more opportunities in scale-up interconnects. The company expects the acquisition to begin contributing revenue in the second half of fiscal 2028.

That said, Marvell's expansion into optical doesn't end with Celestial AI. The company also announced an expanded agreement with GlobalFoundries to increase production capacity for semiconductors used in high-speed optical connections.

With that, Marvell is better positioned to offer a full connectivity stack. Its portfolio now spans optical links, switching, PCIe, and CXL, helping AI systems move data more efficiently as workloads become more demanding.

Taken together, Marvell's portfolio appears better aligned with the complexities of AI infrastructure, from custom silicon and optical connectivity to memory interfaces. And demand for these components will only pick up as AI clusters scale, giving Marvell a much stronger growth outlook.

Is Marvell stock still a buy after the pullback?

Marvell stock experienced a sharp pullback from its 2026 high, but its investment case is still intact. Wall Street agrees, pricing the stock at a generous 37 times forward earnings.

Data center demand remains strong, custom silicon is becoming a bigger growth driver, and Marvell is expanding its connectivity business. Plus, add in its growing relationships with major hyperscalers and new technologies from recent acquisitions.

With its broadening portfolio, the company has multiple ways to benefit from the AI build-out, especially as AI systems scale. That's why, for investors with $10,000, Marvell looks like a compelling place to put it. This pullback serves as a timely opportunity to buy more Marvell shares, adding some breathing room under a heavy valuation.

news.Title: Arm Holdings Has a $4.9 Billion Business Model on Trial. Here’s What It Means for ARM Stock.
news.Content:
Arm Holdings (ARM) faces a new dilemma for a company sitting at the center of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. As its technology becomes more important, one of its biggest customers is fighting over how much it should cost. That fight is now in court.

Qualcomm (QCOM) and Arm have returned to a Delaware courtroom, with Qualcomm seeking to stop royalty payments to Arm for as long as five years. The stakes are potentially worth billions of dollars, while a separate part of the case is testing how Arm can price its newer chip architecture. Arm's royalty business model is a major reason it can keep growing.

So what will this trial cost Arm, and does that mean it is time to dump ARM stock? Let's find out.

More News from Barchart

'When You Say I Should Pay $100 Billion, Then I'm Starting To Do A Little Math': Bill Gates Said He'd Happily Pay 'Over $10 Billion In Taxes' But Some Are Asking Too Much

How to Play Rivian Stock as RIVN Keeps Falling Despite Record Deliveries

Dan Ives Calls SpaceX's $40B Nvidia Chip Debt Plan a 'Smart Move'

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

Why Qualcomm's Challenge Matters So Much to Arm?

Arm Holdings' business model follows a simple concept. Customers pay Arm to use its technology, including CPU designs and other intellectual property. When chips using that technology are eventually shipped, Arm generally receives a royalty. This business model gains traction as Arm's architecture spreads into high-volume markets. If more chips are made using Arm's technology, the royalty opportunity will keep growing.

ARM stock's roughly 148% YTD rally shows that, despite the trial, investors have not abandoned the Arm growth story. This is because Arm generated $4.92 billion of revenue in fiscal 2026, an increase of 23% year over year (YOY). Royalty revenue was $2.61 billion, while licensing revenue reached $2.31 billion. Both businesses grew more than 20% from the year earlier.

Qualcomm is one of Arm's largest customers, having licensed Arm's CPU design for use in its Snapdragon CPUs. Qualcomm is essentially turning to the court for relief that will allow it to stop paying Arm royalties for up to five years.

The Dispute Is Really About Arm's Pricing Power

Qualcomm is challenging how Arm has sought to negotiate pricing for its next-generation architecture. According to Reuters, during the proceedings, Qualcomm's side highlighted an alleged 18,500% increase in royalty rates between Arm's version 9 and version 10 architecture. Qualcomm's older agreement with Arm dates back to 2013, which included a royalty cap of $1.88 per chip for chips with at least five CPU cores. Arm's lawyers questioned whether that arrangement still makes economic sense in a market where some modern data-center processors can contain hundreds of CPU cores.

Story Continues

This makes sense as Arm is no longer operating in a world where its technology is primarily associated with just small smartphone processors. Its architecture is moving deeper into servers, AI infrastructure, automotive systems, edge computing, and other increasingly valuable workloads.

If Arm can successfully charge more for increasingly sophisticated technology, the royalty business model becomes much more powerful. However, if each of its major customers, like Qualcomm, starts challenging it to pay the older, lower rates as chips become more advanced, Arm's long-term growth story could be constrained.

What the Qualcomm Trial Means for ARM Stock

For now, Arm's financial performance gives investors some breathing room. The company's momentum from fiscal 2026 continued into its June quarter. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, revenue reached $1.29 billion, up 22% from the year-ago quarter. Royalty revenue climbed 22% YOY to $715 million, while licensing revenue rose 23% to $574 million. Adjusted earnings per share increased 29% year over year to $0.45.

Concerning royalty revenue, management highlighted that data center royalty revenue more than doubled year over year in the June quarter. That implies that the company is gradually becoming less dependent on the traditional smartphone market and gaining exposure to a much larger AI infrastructure opportunity. So the main concern for Arm currently is that Qualcomm's case will limit its ability to boost royalty prices as chips get more complex. Qualcomm wants to withhold royalty payments for up to five years, and a verdict against Arm might affect how the company negotiates with other big clients. However, if Arm successfully defends its contracts and pricing model, the trial may boost the company's capacity to capitalize on the expansion of AI and data-center computing.

Should Investors Dump ARM Stock Now?

The Qualcomm trial is certainly a real threat to Arm's royalty model, but that doesn't mean it's time to sell ARM stock. Arm's revenue and royalty business continue to grow, and the expanding data center opportunity offers a significant source of growth for the company. Unless the court ruling materially weakens Arm's ability to collect royalties or price its newer technology, the trial is more of a risk that investors need to watch than a reason to abandon the stock.

For now, ARM stock still holds a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating on Wall Street. Among the 32 analysts covering the stock, 20 rate it as a "Strong Buy," three say it is a "Moderate Buy," eight rate it a "Hold," and one recommends a "Strong Sell." The stock has surpassed its average target price of $292.72, while the highest price estimate of $480 indicates a possible 63% rally over the next 12 months.

news.Title: Q3 Earnings Could Blow Past Consensus—Be Ready for What Comes Next
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Palo Alto Networks, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

S&P 500 earnings growth is expected to slow in Q3, but substantial upside surprises in Q1 and Q2 leave room for another beat.

Cybersecurity stocks, including Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, and Okta, are seeing accelerating revenue growth and rising analyst price targets as AI drives security demand.

Marvell raised long-term guidance at its Oct. 6 Investor Day, while analysts have grown increasingly bullish on Intel and AMD amid rising CPU demand for AI inference.

Average S&P 500 earnings typically beat consensus in Q3, as the market has historically done. The S&P 500 tends to outperform by a modest single-digit figure, but that's not the case in 2026. Average earnings could again blow past consensus because results to date reveal a disconnect. Q1 outperformance topped about 1,500 basis points (bps), and Q2 widened the gap to roughly 2,700 bps, a trend that could continue this quarter.

Consensus in early October is for a slowdown to about 29.5% growth, down from roughly 50% in Q2. Given the robust outperformance in Q1 and Q2, trends such as AI and high oil prices, and the relatively modest increase in Q3 estimates, the odds favor another beat. A move into the +50% range would require another unusually large upside surprise.

→ 3 Stocks Chopped in Half: Why These Drops May Be Structural, Not a Dip

Cybersecurity Stocks Flip the SaaS-Pocalypse Narrative

SaaS-Pocalypse fears, fear of AI disrupting software providers across the board, including cybersecurity stocks, were increasingly looking misplaced. The narrative in late 2026 is that AI, and more specifically agentic automation, is driving business for vendors across the board, especially for cybersecurity stocks. Agentic AI drives a sharp increase in traffic and security needs at all levels, with no aspect unimportant. This has made unified cybersecurity platforms and ecosystem partners increasingly in demand, as reflected in analysts' revisions.

→ Q3 Earnings Could Blow Past Consensus—Be Ready for What Comes Next

Analysts are aggressively increasing price targets for cybersecurity stocks. Companies like Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ: PANW), the industry-leading pure-play, CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD), and Okta (NASDAQ: OKTA) are seeing revenue growth accelerate, with internals pointing to momentum and potential for outperformance over the next several years. NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) is among the drivers, especially with its GPUs and industry-specific focus on security, partnering with a variety of technology providers to embed security throughout its AI ecosystem.

Story Continues

→ Why Wall Street Expects Even More From SanDisk After Its 575% Rally

Cybersecurity demand is broad-based across industries and verticals. PANW's CEO Nikesh Arora estimates that $1 trillion of legacy security infrastructure needs to be modernized for the AI era. Systems installed even a few years ago can't handle the speed and scale of attacks, which are lightning-fast and target every available pathway, with multiple agents often working cooperatively to exploit vulnerabilities. This sets the stage for strong, accelerating, and sustained cybersecurity demand.

Marvell Aggressively Ups Targets, Provides Multiyear Visibility to AI Spending

Marvell (NASDAQ: MRVL) raised eyebrows at its Oct. 6 Investor Day by lifting long-term guidance. The company raised guidance for its next fiscal year by 10%-20% and more aggressively raised longer-term forecasts, targeting a 4x increase over the next four years and indicating broad-based strength in its data center products.

While not an increase to this quarter's estimates, it reaffirms the trends in place, including robust growth and acceleration driven by industry-wide demand. Marvell's specific strengths lie in its custom silicon and optical interconnect products. It helps clients build specialized AI factories, removing data bottlenecks so they can monetize the investment.

Marvell's analyst trends are more than suggestive, with earnings estimates moving higher alongside a wave of post-Investor Day price-target increases. They've lifted the consensus, setting a high bar, but several new targets sit well above the average target.

CPU Strength Signals the Age of Inference

Inference reached a critical turning point this year, overtaking model building as the number one demand driver for AI infrastructure. It is expected to continue taking share over time, topping 4x the modeling demand by 2030, and this is being reflected in CPU demand. Inference, such as that driven by Meta's (NASDAQ: META) Muse personal agent, requires lots of feedback, thought processes, and loops, which require complex orchestration. CPUs provide the orchestration layer and are in high demand because they enable this large, growing market.

Analysts, meanwhile, are raising their targets and expectations for companies like Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) and Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD), which command the CPU market. They cite an expanding total addressable market (TAM), sold-out capacity, and the underlying driver—an AI factory buildout. Each AI factory drives demand for numerous inference-focused facilities, underpinning demand for AI infrastructure and security across the ecosystem.

Intel's analyst trends and AMD's analyst forecasts are bullish, particularly around AI-driven demand and higher revenue expectations. With AMD also expected to report its first rack-scale sales, it is positioned to lead in growth and outperformance. AMD's Helios systems are already in production, with deployments beginning in the second half of 2026. Analysts forecast only moderately high growth for AMD over the next five to six quarters, peaking in the low triple-digit range, which seems unlikely given the trends. A more likely scenario is that AMD's Helios launch triggers a wave of demand not yet priced into its stock or that of its ecosystem partners.

news.Title: KLA Returned More Cash Than It Generated Last Quarter. Is That a Problem?
news.Content:
KLA Corporation (NASDAQ: KLAC ) returned $876.3 million to shareholders in its fiscal fourth quarter while generating $817.1 million of free cash flow. The $59.2 million difference invites a capital-allocation question, but one quarter is too short a window to judge whether distributions are sustainable. KLA ranked sixteenth in our recent 20-year performance list. Find which chip-equipment stocks ranked ahead of it and how wide the historical compounding gap became .

The July 28 results showed a better balance across fiscal 2026: $3.77 billion of free cash flow against $3.35 billion of shareholder returns. The annual surplus was $420 million. Investors therefore need to distinguish temporary distribution timing from a payout policy that persistently exceeds cash generation.

For illustration purposes only: a semiconductor manufacturing facility.

Buybacks give management room to adjust

Combined dividends and repurchases consumed 88.9% of annual free cash flow. Repurchases offer discretion if the cycle weakens, making total shareholder returns more flexible than a fixed obligation.

In a simple stress case, a 20% decline in annual free cash flow would leave $3.02 billion. Maintaining the same $3.35 billion distribution would then require $334 million from existing resources or financing. Cutting repurchases could close the gap. This is a policy sensitivity, not an earnings forecast.

Dividends alone consumed $1.06 billion, leaving $2.71 billion of annual free cash flow before repurchases. Under the same 20% cash decline, the dividend would still be covered 2.8 times. The combined payout can therefore become uncovered well before the dividend does. The first adjustment available to management is the pace of discretionary purchases, rather than an immediate need to cut the dividend.

Our Broadcom dividend analysis tests the same distinction between payment safety and the return available at the share price .

Coverage doesn't establish the right repurchase price

At the October 8 close, KLA's equity value was $256.72 billion, close to 68 times fiscal 2026 free cash flow. An affordable repurchase can still deliver a disappointing return if the company pays for growth that later fades. The cash-flow denominator also leaves stock compensation as an economic cost for existing owners.

Fiscal-year net income of $4.83 billion exceeded free cash flow by $1.06 billion. Investors should investigate that conversion gap rather than value repurchases using earnings alone. Cash committed to receivables, inventories and investment cannot simultaneously retire shares. At the quoted equity value, $2.29 billion of annual repurchases represents less than 1% of capitalization before any dilution, illustrating why a large dollar program may produce only a modest ownership benefit.

Story Continues

Our Lam Research–KLA comparison examines the price investors pay for each company's cash generation and the growth needed to justify it .

Insider Monkey's database showed 81 hedge-fund holders in Q2 2026, up from 71 in Q1. Arrowstreet reduced its split-adjusted share position 40.4%. KLA's full-year cash generation covered its distributions, so the quarterly shortfall alone is a weak bearish argument. The stronger test is whether future cash growth supports both the payout policy and attractive repurchase economics as equipment demand changes.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of KLAC as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame.
